inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 791,480,489 shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (792,283,683 issued less 803,194 treasury, H1-2026 note 20) plus 689,779 equity-settled Performance Shares (H1-2026 EPS note) = 792.2m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Airbus is a repurchaser (EUR565m FY2025, EUR276m FY2024, EUR334m FY2023 - largely to neutralise ESOP issuance), so the flat count is funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back 'Share-based payment (IFRS 2)' (kpis StockBasedComp 335). No separate cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed; ESOP and performance-share plans are equity-settled, so 335 is used as the combined figure.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:17Z Xetra regular close (Yahoo meta currency EUR, exchange GER)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR build: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~8.2%; group is net cash so WACC ~ cost of equity, rounded to 8.5% for long-duration, USD-priced/EUR-cost revenue. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality and execution risk are charged in the bear flows and the weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: reported FCF (OCF - capex) is post-IFRS-16 and lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; lease liabilities (EUR2,380m at FY2025) sit inside Airbus's financing liabilities and are therefore subtracted once via net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI is immaterial (EUR88m book at 30 June 2026) and deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Airbus's own net cash position at 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 note 21): gross cash EUR23,376m (cash 9,499 + current securities 2,795 + non-current securities 11,082) less financing liabilities 4,851 + 9,425 and interest-rate contracts 740 = net cash EUR8,360m. Securities are included because they are treasury liquidity, and their interest income is stripped from the owner-FCF base. FY2025 year-end net cash was EUR12,171m; the June figure is the seasonal low after the EUR2,530m dividend.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Airbus is an operating industrial (commercial aircraft ~72%, defence & space ~18%, helicopters ~12%); no prior valuation or memory entry exists, so this is a fresh build. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported OCF-capex 4,031 - SBC 335 - interest income 710 = 2,986. Note OCF also bears ~651 of interest paid, so last_fcf is conservative as a reference; the projections are an unlevered component build (EBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> tax -> capex -> WC), with gross debt and gross liquidity both in the bridge. FY0 EBITDA is REPORTED EBIT + D&A (9,215, 12.6%), not EBIT Adjusted; the forward EBITDA margin path is before SBC and sits ~0.5-0.7pp below Airbus's adjusted basis to absorb the recurring 'adjustments' (programme charges, restructuring, FX mismatches) that averaged ~EUR0.6bn/yr FY2023-25. The FY2025 EUR749m Spirit AeroSystems charge (A220 impairment + onerous contracts) is treated as non-recurring and NOT carried in the margin path. FY2026 year-1 calibration: revenue +9% (870 delivery guide vs 793; H1 revenue +12%), implied EBIT ~EUR7.0bn reported vs EUR7.5bn adjusted guide, owner FCF ~EUR4.1bn vs the EUR4.5bn FCF-before-customer-financing guide (which is pre-SBC). Working capital is negative capture (-8% of revenue increase): inventory for the rate ramps outruns pre-delivery-payment inflows. Pension provisions sit inside non-current provisions (3,829 total) and are largely funded through CTAs; not separately bridged. Equity-method stakes (MBDA, ATR, ArianeGroup) earn inside EBIT and are therefore not added to the bridge.

equity_bridge.item: Reverse H1 FY2026 FCF before customer financing already deducted from the June net-cash anchor
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 FCF before customer financing was -EUR1,166m; it reduced the 30 June net cash and is also inside the full-year FY2026 year-1 flow, so it is added back once to avoid double-counting the seasonal H1 burn.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (26-32%) diverges >30% from revenue (8%) and EPS (7%) CAGRs: book value is rebuilding off the FY2020 COVID trough and swings with the hedge-reserve mark-to-market (EUR-912m in H1 2026 alone), so it is not a usable growth proxy. Revenue 5yr CAGR selected and decelerated.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020 EPS and FCF were negative (COVID), so 5-year EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined. Owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - SBC - interest income): FY2023 2,308; FY2024 2,621; FY2025 2,986. FY2022 owner FCF (3,753) deducts SBC only because gross interest income was not split out before FY2023 (net interest result was -232), which flatters the start point and makes the -7.3% 3yr owner-FCF CAGR worse than the like-for-like trend (+13.7%/yr FY2023-25). The reported-vs-owner gap reflects interest income on the cash pile far more than SBC, which is small (0.46% of revenue) though it grew from 31 (FY2016) to 335 (FY2025).

base.narrative: Guidance delivered and the rate ramps land roughly on the revised timetable.

bull.narrative: Engines unblock, A320 at 75/month by end-2027, defence re-rates margins.

bear.narrative: Engine shortages persist, airline down-cycle in year 4, Spirit/space overruns.

scenario_narratives.base: Airbus delivers the FY2026 guide (~870 aircraft, EBIT Adjusted ~EUR7.5bn, FCF before customer financing ~EUR4.5bn) and the A320 Family reaches 70-75/month around end-2027 as Pratt & Whitney GTF supply slowly normalises, with A220 to 13/month and A350 to 12/month by 2028. Revenue compounds ~8% for three years on the record 9,222-aircraft backlog then decelerates to ~3% as rates plateau. Operating leverage on the ramp plus Defence & Space recovery lift reported EBIT margin from ~8.7% to ~10.6% by 2030 (EBITDA before SBC 15.3%), then hold. Capex steps down from the Spirit/rate-ramp peak (5.3% of revenue) to 4.5%; the ramp keeps consuming working capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: Engine supply unblocks faster than feared and Boeing's 737 MAX/787 recovery remains slow, letting Airbus sell every slot it can build at firmer pricing: A320 at 75/month by end-2027, widebody demand lifts A350/A330 rates, and the in-housed Spirit work packages cut structure costs. European rearmament drives record Defence & Space intake at improving margins and the Leonardo/Thales satellite combination ends the OneSat-type losses. Revenue grows ~10% for three years, reported EBIT margin reaches ~12% (EBITDA before SBC 16.5%), and the terminal exit is a modestly richer 16x.
scenario_narratives.bear: GTF and LEAP engine shortages keep pushing A320 Family rate targets out, Spirit integration absorbs more cost than the EUR749m already booked, and Space Systems produces another programme charge. Around year 4 an airline down-cycle (recession, fuel spike or credit tightening for lessors) triggers deferrals that the backlog cushions but does not prevent: revenue falls 3% and EBITDA margin troughs at 12% (reported EBIT ~7%) with D&A and capex sticky. Recovery is to a lower 13% EBITDA margin as COMAC's C919 starts to cap narrowbody pricing in China, with a cyclical 13x exit and 2% terminal growth. The business stays solidly cash generative - this is a margin-and-timing bear, not a solvency bear (net cash EUR8.4bn).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because the ramp depends on a supplier (Pratt & Whitney) Airbus does not control and commercial aerospace is cyclical over a 10-year horizon, with no solvency risk to push it higher. Base at 50% because the record backlog and duopoly structure make the guided path the most likely one. Bull trimmed to 25% from 35% because it needs several independent things to go right at once - engine supply, Boeing staying weak, defence margins and a space fix.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Airbus as a cyclical duopoly industrial on an unlevered owner-FCF basis, anchored to reported (not adjusted) EBIT so recurring 'one-offs' are paid for, with the ramp's working-capital and capex intensity charged explicitly and cyclicality carried in a meaningful bear weight rather than a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Engine supply (P&W GTF, CFM LEAP) gating A320 Family rates - each year of delay pushes the margin ramp right
Terminal value carries most of the value; a 15x cap on a cyclical is the binding judgment
USD-priced revenue against a EUR cost base: hedge book protects ~3 years, beyond that FX moves margins
Working-capital intensity of the ramp (H1 2026 FCF before customer financing -EUR1.2bn) - a bigger inventory build would cut near-term FCF
Defence & Space programme charges (OneSat, A400M legacy) and Spirit purchase-price allocation still open through end-2026
